title: The scored `environment` component is credited to nobody: no `sourceBreakdown` entry, no `sources` line, and the guard test hardcodes the pre-v3.9 four-key set
evidence:
`build_source_breakdown()` returns exactly `prov['breakdown']`. I dumped it for every city:

  python -c "...; [print(c, sorted(p['breakdown'])) for c,p in m.CITY_PROVENANCE.items()]"
  london ['afford', 'growth', 'live', 'quiet']   (identical for all 13 cities)

`build_sources()` (app.py:4938) likewise names no environment source. London's array resolves to: NaPTAN, NHS ODS, postcodes.io/NSPL, borough metadata (ONS + DfE), "Aviation noise context: DEFRA strategic noise mapping". No DEFRA background pollution maps, no DEFRA road Lden, no Environment Agency RoFRS — the three datasets that are the ENTIRE `environment` component (`_ENV_WEIGHTS` app.py:5276, `aq_to_score`/`road_to_score`/`flood_to_score` app.py:5349/5375/5360), which carries 0.14 of six personas and 0.18 of `family` and `laterlife` (app.py:252-265).

The published claims this contradicts:
- terms.html:292 (contractual): "Every API response includes a `sources` array naming the datasets used to produce it. If you display or redistribute Sky Score data, you must carry that attribution through to your own users."
- METHODOLOGY.md:1892 (§18): "Every `/v1/score` response carries a `sources` array and a `sourceBreakdown` object naming the origin of **each scored component**."
- METHODOLOGY.md:1896: "Where a component has no source, the response is required to say so rather than publish a silent default."

The code applies exactly this standard to itself elsewhere — app.py:4665 explains NaPTAN and NHS ODS were added on 2026-08-25 because they "supplied 0.35 of London's liveability weight since v3.6/v3.7 with no credit - and OGL v3.0 requires attribution."

The guard is inverted. backend/tests/test_score.py:1243:

  self.assertEqual(
      set(app.build_source_breakdown(city)),
      {'quiet', 'afford', 'growth', 'live'},
      f'{city} breakdown must cover every scored component',
  )

I ran `python -m pytest backend/tests/test_score.py -k every_city_has_its_own_provenance -q` → 1 passed.
failure_scenario: A B2B integrator scores any London postcode, takes the returned `sources` array, and republishes it to their own users exactly as terms.html §6 obliges them to. The array they carry forward credits DfT, NHS, ONS, DfE and DEFRA-aviation but omits DEFRA's background pollution maps, DEFRA's road Lden surface and the Environment Agency's RoFRS — the sole basis for 14-18% of the number they are republishing. Both the integrator and Sky Score are then distributing OGL v3.0 data with no attribution, while METHODOLOGY §18 tells the integrator's auditor the array is complete. A conveyancer auditing `sourceBreakdown` for the `env` value in `components` finds no key for it at all, and METHODOLOGY §18 says that state means the component has no source — which is false; it has three.
why_gates_miss_it: `test_every_city_has_its_own_provenance` is the only gate over provenance completeness and it asserts a hardcoded literal `{'quiet','afford','growth','live'}` under a message claiming it covers every scored component. It passed unchanged through v3.9 (2026-08-26) and v4.0 (2026-08-29), and it would go RED on the fix — adding an `env` breakdown key fails the assertEqual. Every other preflight stage (32 of them) checks lint, markup, a11y, responsiveness, data-vs-publisher parity or site-vs-Lambda score parity; none reads the `sources`/`sourceBreakdown` contract. `test_non_uk_city_never_credits_uk_bodies` only checks that NYC does NOT name UK bodies, never that a UK city names the right ones.
suggested_fix: Add an `env` key to every city's `breakdown` naming DEFRA background pollution maps (PCM), DEFRA Round 4 road Lden and EA RoFRS with the weight each carries, plus `sources` lines for the three (and the NYC/Cardiff 'component declined' case). Then replace the hardcoded set in test_score.py:1243 with one derived from the components the engine can actually emit — e.g. assert the breakdown keys equal the keys `score_borough()` can put in `components` — so the gate cannot go stale on the next component.

title: The live OpenAPI spec declares `enum: [london, nyc]` in four places, so a spec-validating client rejects 11 of the 13 cities the API serves
evidence:
Four `enum: [london, nyc]` sites, verified live rather than from source:

  curl -s https://skyscore.co.uk/score-demo/openapi.yaml -o /tmp/live-openapi.yaml   # 200
  diff -q /tmp/live-openapi.yaml score-demo/openapi.yaml   # identical
  grep -c 'enum: \[london, nyc\]' /tmp/live-openapi.yaml   # 4

- line 374 — the `city` QUERY PARAMETER on `GET /v1/score`
- line 716 — `RegionsResponse.cities[].id`
- line 822 — `Location.city`, present on every score response
- line 903 — the `city` field of each item in a `/v1/score/batch` request

Against the live service:

  curl -s .../prod/v1/regions | python -c "...print([c['id'] for c in d['cities']])"
  ['london','nyc','westmidlands','westyorkshire','southyorkshire','merseyside',
   'tyneandwear','leicester','teesside','bristol','cardiff','nottingham','manchester']

This is the same defect the file itself records having fixed once already, for personas (openapi.yaml:641): "Three enums in this spec listed personas and only one was complete, so a spec-validating client would have rejected renter, commuter and laterlife - valid requests and valid responses." The personas were fixed; the cities were not.
failure_scenario: An integrator generates a client from the published spec (which is the stated purpose — README lists it as "OpenAPI 3.0 spec" and it is rendered at /score-demo/api-docs.html). The generated `City` type has two members. `GET /v1/score?postcode=M1 1AE` returns `location.city: "manchester"`, which fails deserialisation or response validation; `GET /v1/regions` fails on 11 of 13 array elements; and the generated client physically cannot send `?city=manchester` for a borough-name lookup such as `?borough=Salford&city=manchester`, which the live API answers 200. The integrator concludes Sky Score covers two cities, exactly the opposite of what pricing.html and api/index.html sell.
why_gates_miss_it: No preflight stage parses openapi.yaml. `html-validate` and `a11y-source` cover markup only; `check_deploy_drift.sh` compares deployed bytes against source bytes and both are equally stale (I confirmed they are byte-identical). The only tests that touch the spec (`test_404_wording_is_the_shipped_string`, `test_live_response_location_keys_unchanged`) grep for one 404 string and assert Location's key NAMES — neither reads an enum. `tests/smoke-local.mjs` asserts CITY_DATA key parity in the frontend, not the spec.
suggested_fix: Replace all four enums with a plain `type: string` plus a description pointing at `/v1/regions` as the authoritative list, and add a preflight stage that loads the spec and asserts every enum of city ids is either absent or equal to `sorted(app.CITIES)` — derived from the engine, not restated in the spec.

The `quiet` description at :757 additionally states "Aircraft ONLY - road noise is a map layer on the consumer site and is not a score input" — false at v4.0. Confirmed live (byte-identical download, see the enum finding).

2. api/index.html:224, confirmed live with `curl -s https://skyscore.co.uk/api/`:
   "Single composite + four components: quiet, affordability, growth, liveability."
   And the "30-second sample" at :253-266, explicitly captioned "shape and field names as the live API emits them":
     "components": { "quiet": 5.0, "afford": 7.2, "growth": 7.8, "live": 7.2 },
     "weights": { "quiet": 0.22, "afford": 0.22, "growth": 0.0, "live": 0.56 },
     "methodologyVersion": "3.8"
   The live `family` weights are `{'quiet': 0.18, 'afford': 0.18, 'growth': 0.00, 'live': 0.46, 'env': 0.18}` (app.py:254). Live methodologyVersion is 4.0.

3. score-demo/index.html:589-593 — the demo README calls "Try it in 30 seconds" — renders exactly four bars:
     ${compRow('quiet','Quiet')} ${compRow('afford','Affordability')}
     ${compRow('growth','Growth')} ${compRow('live','Liveability')}
   `compRow` prints "weight NN%" from `d.weights[key]`. For `balanced` those four sum to 0.86.
failure_scenario: A prospect runs the browser demo on a London postcode. They see Quiet 32%, Affordability 27%, Growth 0%, Liveability 27% — 86% — and a headline score they cannot reproduce from the bars shown, because 14% of it (the environment component, which just moved the median environment score by more than a point) is invisible. They then read api/index.html, which tells them the product has four components, and generate a client from the OpenAPI spec, whose `Components` and `Weights` schemas have no `env` property. suggested_fix: Add `env` to the openapi `Components`/`Weights`/`sourceBreakdown` schemas (leaving it out of `required`, since it is legitimately omitted for NYC and Cardiff), correct the `quiet` description, re-capture the api/index.html sample from a live call rather than editing values by hand, and add `${compRow('env','Environment')}` to score-demo guarded on the key's presence. Then add a preflight stage asserting that the union of keys the engine can emit in `components` appears in the spec's Components schema.

title: README's v4.0 headline says 90 of 99 boroughs are "fully measured" for environment; the code says 85, and README's own three numbers sum to 104
evidence:
README.md:17-21, added with the v4.0 commit:

  "With it, **90 of 99 boroughs are fully measured**, 5 are partial (Teesside,
   awaiting one flood tile) and 9 are unavailable (New York's 5 ...; Cardiff's 4 ...)."

90 + 5 + 9 = 104, against a stated denominator of 99.

Counted through the Lambda's own `env_resolution()` over all 13 borough registries:

  python -c "...; cnt[m.env_resolution(bd).split(' ')[0]] += 1 ..."
  total boroughs 99
  Counter({'measured': 85, 'unavailable': 9, 'partial': 5})
  partial   = Teesside x5
  unavailable = NYC x5 + Cardiff x4

So 90 is the count of boroughs that get a PUBLISHED environment score (85 measured + 5 partial), relabelled as "fully measured". METHODOLOGY.md §4.7 (:843) and §20 (:1921) both carry the correct 85/5/9 — the same wave got it right in one document and wrong in the other.

I also reproduced the surrounding numbers to make sure only this one is off: median environment 8.0 -> 6.7 under the v3.9 vs v4.0 weights (README says 8.00 -> 6.65), and exactly 4 boroughs rose (Kingston upon Thames, Doncaster, Sefton, South Tyneside), which README states correctly.
failure_scenario: README is the first page of the source-available repo the methodology audit is run against, and its first screen is the v4.0 summary. A reader takes "90 of 99 fully measured" as the coverage figure and cites it, when 5 of those 90 are Teesside boroughs scored on two inputs of three with no flood data at all — the exact boroughs the v4.0 floor was raised to stop over-ranking. Anyone who adds the three numbers up gets 104 against a stated 99 and loses confidence in every other figure in the file.
why_gates_miss_it: No gate reads README.md. The `env_resolution()` counts are not asserted anywhere outside `EnvironmentComponentTests`' unit cases for the ramps and the floor; nothing counts the population. The closest precedent in the repo — METHODOLOGY's "84 of 99" liveability figure, which I verified reproduces exactly — is described as "re-counted through the scoring Lambda's own live_resolution()", but that is a manual recount, not a check.
suggested_fix: Correct README.md:18 to "85 of 99 boroughs are fully measured, 5 are partial and 9 unavailable". Better: make both coverage figures generated — a small script that prints the `env_resolution()`/`live_resolution()` histogram, run as a preflight stage that fails when the numbers in README.md and METHODOLOGY.md do not match what it counted, so the next city cannot silently stale them.

title: ?compare=previous explains every score under the balanced persona, so a non-balanced request gets an explanation that contradicts its own scoreChange
evidence:
build_comparison() hardcodes the balanced weight set for both the decomposition and the prose, while resolve_query() scored the borough with the caller's weights:

  app.py:386   current, previous, city, PERSONAS['balanced'], name, cur_bm, prev_bm, cur_ranks, prev_ranks
  app.py:398   'attribution': build_attribution(current, previous, PERSONAS['balanced']),

build_attribution then does `for key, weight in weights.items(): ... if weight == 0: continue` (app.py:429-440) and build_why puts every zero-weight component into `unweighted` with the note "it carries no weight in this view" (app.py:634-651).

Ran:
  python -c "...; body,_ = app.resolve_query({'borough':'Barking and Dagenham','city':'london','persona':'investor','compare':'previous'})"
Output (verbatim):
  weights {'quiet':0.09,'afford':0.26,'growth':0.34,'live':0.17,'env':0.14}
  score 8.8  previousScore 7.1  scoreChange 1.7
  attribution []
  why.headline: 'Score unchanged at 8.8, even though the market moved.'
  why.unweighted[0].note: 'Growth moved from 5.0 to 10.0 out of 10, but it carries no weight in this view, so it did not change the score.'
  why.caveats[0]: 'Growth moved this quarter but is not counted in this view - it is weighted only for the investor persona...'

Same effect with weights that merely differ from balanced. For Camden with persona=family the attribution publishes `weight: 0.27` for afford while the response's own `weights` field says 0.18, and build_why appends: 'The drivers sum to -0.08 against a published change of +0.0; the 0.08 difference is rounding in the per-factor values, not a missing driver.' Both `persona` and `compare` are documented, independent query parameters (score-demo/openapi.yaml:376 and :410).
failure_scenario: GET /v1/score?borough=Barking%20and%20Dagenham&city=london&persona=investor&compare=previous returns score 8.8, comparison.previousScore 7.1 and comparison.scoreChange 1.7, and in the same object comparison.explanation reads "Score unchanged at 8.8, even though the market moved." followed by "Growth moved from 5.0 to 10.0 out of 10, but it carries no weight in this view, so it did not change the score" and "it is weighted only for the investor persona" - served to a caller who asked for the investor persona, where growth carries 0.34 and drove the whole +1.7. comparison.attribution is an empty array, so the decomposition whose stated purpose is "the parts must add up to the whole, and a caller can check it" cites no driver at all. For family/quietlife/renter/commuter/firsttime/laterlife and for any accepted custom weight set the array is non-empty but carries balanced's weights and contributions, and the residual caveat actively denies the real cause ("rounding in the per-factor values, not a missing driver") when the missing driver is a real weighted component.
why_gates_miss_it: No test in the repo ever passes a persona alongside compare - verified by `grep -rn "'compare'" backend/tests/*.py tests/*.py`, which returns 7 hits, every one of them using the default (balanced) persona. test_compare_previous_includes_attribution (backend/tests/test_score.py:544) calls resolve_query({'borough':'Ealing','compare':'previous'}) with no persona, and test_attribution_contributions_reconcile_to_score_change (test_score.py:222) checks /v1/changes, which is balanced-only by construction (app.py:6858 `bal = PERSONAS['balanced']`). So the reconciliation gate only ever samples the one persona where the hardcode happens to be correct - an expectation that agrees with the code under test. scripts/check_score_sanity.py sends neither `persona` nor `compare` (grep returns no match for either). The frontend never calls compare, so tests/borough-score-parity.mjs and tests/site-api-parity.mjs cannot see it.
suggested_fix: Thread the caller's weight set through: give build_comparison a `weights` parameter and pass the same `weights` object resolve_query used for calc_score (app.py:6656-6663) into both build_attribution and build_why. handle_changes keeps passing PERSONAS['balanced'] explicitly because it genuinely is a balanced-only surface. Add a test that runs resolve_query for each of the eight personas with compare=previous and asserts abs(scoreChange - sum(contribution)) stays inside roundingResidual, and that build_why's `unweighted` list is empty whenever the requested persona weights that component.

title: A DynamoDB read failure makes /v1/environment and /v1/score assert that DEFRA has no contour at a postcode DEFRA has measured

  app.NOISE_RASTER_TABLE='london-flight-map-noise-raster'; app._get_ddb_client=lambda: None

  -> context.quietResolution 'postcode', coverage.quiet.measuredAtLocation False, coverage.notices carrying the identical sentence, and every environment reading (roadNoiseLdenDb, no2AnnualMeanUgm3, pm25AnnualMeanUgm3) silently absent.

title: The liveability-unavailable coverage notice has never been emitted: build_coverage compares against a bare 'unavailable' that live_resolution has never returned
evidence:
build_coverage tests for an exact string:
  app.py:5650   if live_source == 'unavailable':
  app.py:5651       notices.append(_LIVE_UNAVAILABLE_NOTICE)
live_resolution has never returned that bare token. Today it returns f'unavailable — {present}/{total} inputs measured, too few to publish; the component is omitted and its weight redistributed' (app.py:5699-5703).

Ran:
  app.build_coverage('borough', app.live_resolution({}, english=True))
  -> {'quiet': {...}, 'live': {'basis': 'unavailable - 0/4 inputs measured, ...', 'measuredAtLocation': False}, 'notices': ['Aircraft noise here is a borough-wide average, ...']}
The live notice is absent even with zero inputs present.

It was born dead. `git log -S"live_source == 'unavailable'"` gives one commit, e531fa6; `git show e531fa6:backend/lambdas/score/app.py` shows the same `== 'unavailable'` test at line 2769 sitting beside a live_resolution that already returned 'unavailable - all inputs defaulted to 5.0 placeholder' (line 2816). Its sibling test on the same two lines, `'measuredAtLocation': live_source == 'measured'` (app.py:5661), works, because 'measured' IS returned bare - which is what makes the dead one look alive on inspection.

The text it guards is also stale: _LIVE_UNAVAILABLE_NOTICE (app.py:5549-5552) says the component "is a neutral placeholder rather than a measurement", describing the 5.0-placeholder behaviour get_live_score removed - live_resolution's own comment at app.py:5709-5713 records that those strings were corrected for exactly that reason, and this one was missed because nothing reaches it. `grep -rn "LIVE_UNAVAILABLE|neutral placeholder" backend/tests tests index.html extension` returns nothing: no test and no consumer.
failure_scenario: A borough drops below two liveability inputs - the code path the design explicitly supports (live_weights_for's docstring: a city "can now be sourced one field at a time"; Nottingham's Broxtowe/Gedling/Rushcliffe already sit at exactly 2/4 with crimeRate and p8 both None, so one ONS or NaPTAN refresh takes them to 1/4). /v1/score then omits the `live` component, redistributes 27-46% of the weight, and returns coverage.notices containing only the aircraft notice. The plain-English surface build_coverage exists to provide - 'Returned on every response... so a consumer surface can show a limitation without having to know what "postcode" means' - says nothing about the missing component, and if the comparison were ever repaired it would then publish a sentence claiming a neutral placeholder was used when the component was dropped instead.
why_gates_miss_it: No test references _LIVE_UNAVAILABLE_NOTICE or coverage['notices'] for the live component (grep returns zero hits across backend/tests, tests, index.html and extension/). No borough in the shipped dataset currently has fewer than 2 live inputs - I enumerated all 99 and the worst is 'partial - 2/4' - so even a data-driven test would not reach the branch. The adjacent `measuredAtLocation` comparison on the same two lines does work, so the pair reads as correct.
suggested_fix: Test the prefix, not the whole string - `if live_source.startswith('unavailable')` - or better, have live_resolution return a (state, text) pair so build_coverage keys on the state rather than on prose that has already been rewritten twice. Update _LIVE_UNAVAILABLE_NOTICE to describe the omit-and-rescale behaviour, and add a test that constructs a 1-of-4 borough record and asserts the notice appears.

title: City of London's sources array claims schools 'falls back to a curated band' while the same response says the input was dropped and its weight redistributed
evidence:
_london_borough_metadata_line emits, for an English borough with no Progress 8:
  app.py:4934   parts.append('no Progress 8 figure published for this area; schools falls back to a curated band')
But live_component_scores does not fall back for an English borough - v3.5 removed the categorical tier, and the code says so explicitly:
  app.py:5175-5177   if english:
                         if bd.get('p8') is not None:
                             scores['schools'] = school_score(bd['p8'])

Ran:
  app.resolve_query({'borough':'City of London','city':'london'})
Output:
  components: {'quiet':7.5,'afford':6.1,'growth':1.0,'live':4.8,'env':2.9}
  context.liveResolution: 'partial - 3/4 inputs measured; the absent inputs are not estimated, their weight is redistributed across the measured ones'
  sources: ['Borough metadata: crime rate is a Sky Score estimate ... and no Progress 8 figure published for this area; schools falls back to a curated band']
  sourceBreakdown['schools']: None
and app.live_component_scores(bd, english=True) returns {'crimeRate': 0.667, 'transport': 10, 'healthcare': 4} - no schools entry at all, despite bd carrying schools='good'. So one payload contains two contradictory statements about the same input: the audited sources array says a curated band was used, liveResolution says the input was not estimated and its 35% was redistributed.

Only London declares _BOROUGH_METADATA_SENTINEL in CITY_PROVENANCE (checked all 13 cities), and City of London is the only London borough with p8 None, so exactly one borough is affected - the same borough this function's docstring was written about.
failure_scenario: A B2B integrator auditing provenance calls GET /v1/score?borough=City of London&city=london and is told in the machine-readable `sources` array that the schools input came from a curated band. No schools input was used: live_component_scores dropped it and live_weights_for redistributed its 0.35 across crime, transport and healthcare, which is why live is 4.8 rather than a schools-weighted figure. The same response's context.liveResolution states the opposite, so the two provenance surfaces disagree inside one payload.
why_gates_miss_it: tests/test_borough_data_parity.py compares data FIELDS between the two holders, not provenance prose. The backend suite asserts liveResolution's counts and asserts that the metadata line names the crime estimate, but nothing cross-checks the sentence against what live_component_scores actually consumed - the sentence is a string, and no gate reads a string against behaviour. The claim is also true-sounding: bd really does carry schools='good', it is simply never read for an English borough.
suggested_fix: Change the branch to say what happens - 'no Progress 8 figure published for this area; the schools input is omitted and its weight redistributed' - and derive it from live_component_scores(bd, english) rather than from `bd.get('p8') is not None`, so the sentence cannot disagree with the scorer. Add a test asserting that whenever 'schools' is absent from live_component_scores the metadata line does not claim a fallback.

title: /v1/changes freezes the postcode-resolution attribution of whichever request warmed the container into a body cached for its whole lifetime
evidence:
handle_changes builds `_CHANGES_BODY` once per container and memoises it (app.py:6820, 6853-6855, 6930-6948). One of the lines it bakes in is runtime state:
  app.py:6947   'sources': build_sources('london'),
build_sources resolves CITY_PROVENANCE callables at call time (app.py:4956-4968), one of which is _postcode_source_line(local_postcode_served()) (app.py:4517-4536), reading the threading.local flag that only resolve_query resets (app.py:6501-6503). handle_changes never calls resolve_query, so the flag it reads belongs to whatever ran before it on the same thread. /v1/score and /v1/changes are the same Lambda function and the same main thread.

Ran:
  app.mark_local_postcode_served(); b = json.loads(app.handle_changes({})['body'])
  -> b['sources'] contains 'Postcode resolution: ONS National Statistics Postcode Lookup (Open Government Licence v3.0), with postcodes.io ... as fallback'
  app.reset_postcode_attribution(); b2 = json.loads(app.handle_changes({})['body'])
  -> b2 still contains the ONS line, because the body is cached.
The reverse also holds: if /v1/changes is the first request on a cold container the body freezes 'Postcode resolution: postcodes.io (Open Government Licence v3.0)' for that container's life, even once NSPL is serving. /v1/changes resolves no postcodes at all, so neither line describes anything it did.
failure_scenario: A warm container serves GET /v1/score?postcode=SW11+1AA (NSPL answers, setting the thread-local flag), then GET /v1/changes. The unauthenticated /v1/changes body credits 'ONS National Statistics Postcode Lookup (Open Government Licence v3.0)' as a source for a borough-level payload that performed no postcode lookup, and every subsequent /v1/changes response from that container repeats it regardless of later state. A different container that happened to serve /v1/changes first publishes the opposite claim for the same deployment, so two callers get contradicting attribution for byte-identical data. This is finding I11 (per-container attribution leak, fixed in resolve_query on 2026-08-22) surviving on the route next door, amplified by the cache.
why_gates_miss_it: ChangesCachingTests (backend/tests/test_handlers.py:709-750) reasons explicitly about which fields may be cached and concludes generatedAt is 'the one field that is genuinely per-response' - it asserts generatedAt is not frozen and asserts the rest of the body is byte-stable, which is exactly what a frozen sources line satisfies. test_attribution_does_not_survive_into_the_next_request (test_score.py:1179) covers resolve_query only. Each test also runs with `self.app._CHANGES_BODY = None` and a fresh thread-local, so the cross-request ordering that produces the defect never occurs in the suite.
suggested_fix: Stamp `sources` per response the way generatedAt already is - keep it out of _CHANGES_BODY and add it in the two return statements alongside generatedAt - or, since /v1/changes performs no postcode resolution, drop the postcode-resolution line from its source list entirely and credit only the bodies that supplied the price and metadata it actually used.

title: liveResolution counts City of London's in-house crime estimate as a measured input, the half of the defect its own comment says was fixed
evidence:
live_resolution's comment states the defect it exists to prevent: 'getting this wrong is what made the City of London report "measured" while its schools input was the retired Ofsted band AND ITS CRIME RATE WAS OUR OWN ESTIMATE' (app.py:5678-5684). The implementation special-cases schools only:
  app.py:5686   def _slot_present(f):
  app.py:5687       if f != 'schools':
  app.py:5688           return bd.get(f) is not None
So crimeRate counts as present whether or not it is ours. City of London's record carries {'crimeEstimated': True, 'crimeRate': 190} (app.py:1273), and `grep -n crimeEstimated backend/lambdas/score/app.py` shows the flag is read in exactly one place - _london_borough_metadata_line (app.py:4921) - and never by live_resolution.

Ran:
  app.resolve_query({'borough':'City of London','city':'london'})['context']['liveResolution']
  -> 'partial - 3/4 inputs measured; the absent inputs are not estimated, their weight is redistributed across the measured ones'
Of those three, one (crimeRate 190, scoring 0.67 through crime_to_score) is a Sky Score estimate that ONS declines to publish. The same field feeds coverage.live.basis (app.py:5657-5660), so the claim is repeated on the plain-English surface.
failure_scenario: GET /v1/score?borough=City of London&city=london returns context.liveResolution and coverage.live.basis both reading 'partial - 3/4 inputs measured', and the sentence goes on to say the absent inputs 'are not estimated'. Two of those three inputs are third-party measurements; the third is an in-house estimate, and it is the highest-weighted of the three at 0.30 of a component whose weight this borough already inflated by dropping schools. A consumer filtering on liveResolution to exclude estimated inputs - the exact use the field is published for - keeps this borough.
why_gates_miss_it: The liveability tests assert the COUNT and the schools half of _slot_present (which was the half that got fixed); none asserts anything about crimeEstimated reaching liveResolution. Only one borough in 99 carries the flag, so a spot check of any other borough agrees with the code. The sources array does disclose the estimate separately, which makes the payload internally inconsistent rather than uniformly wrong and lets each surface look correct in isolation.
suggested_fix: Extend _slot_present the way it already handles schools: `if f == 'crimeRate': return bd.get('crimeRate') is not None and not bd.get('crimeEstimated')`, which takes City of London to 'partial - 2/4' and matches what _london_borough_metadata_line already tells the caller. Add a test asserting that a record with crimeEstimated=True never reports that slot as measured.

title: The demo-key scope gate cannot fail while the demo key is out of monthly quota - and it is out of quota right now
evidence:
`const BLOCKED_STATUS = new Set([403, 429]);` (line 34); checks 2 and 3 assert only `BLOCKED_STATUS.has(r.status)` (lines 99-105, 113-119). API Gateway returns 429 for TWO unrelated reasons and the gate cannot tell them apart. Proven live today:

  curl -H "X-Api-Key: <demo key from score-demo/index.html:449>" .../prod/v1/score?postcode=SW11+1AA
    -> status=429  {"message":"Limit Exceeded"}      <- monthly Quota (Limit: 2000) exhausted
  curl -X POST -H "X-Api-Key: <same>" .../prod/v1/score/batch -d '{"queries":[{"postcode":"SW11 1AA"}]}'
    -> status=429  {"message":"Too Many Requests"}   <- the ScoreDemoUsagePlan RateLimit-0 deny

Running the gate as preflight does (`set -a && . ./.env && node tests/demo-key-scope.mjs`) printed:
  WARN  GET /v1/score not verified - demo quota exhausted (429).
  PASS  POST /v1/score/batch is refused  status=429
  PASS  POST /v1/chat is refused  status=429
  ... OK: the demo key reaches /v1/score and nothing else   EXIT=0

The gate reports quota exhaustion in check 1 and then accepts the identical status code as proof of a different mechanism in checks 2 and 3. It already captures the distinguishing evidence - `call()` reads the body into `r.text` (line 45) - and never looks at it.
failure_scenario: Someone edits `backend/template.yaml` and drops the `/v1/chat/POST` and `/v1/score/batch/POST` Throttle entries from `ScoreDemoUsagePlan` (lines 615-623), or API Gateway changes how it reads RateLimit 0. Because the demo key's 2,000/month quota is currently exhausted, every request with that key returns 429 regardless, so both assertions still print PASS and the file still prints "OK: the demo key reaches /v1/score and nothing else" with exit 0. Preflight reports the stage green. On the 1st of the month the quota resets and the key printed in the page source of score-demo/index.html - which the template's own comment calls "a free LLM for anyone who finds it" - reaches POST /v1/chat (Bedrock, billed to this account) and POST /v1/score/batch (100 scores per request, 20x the Free tier, with no email address given). The one gate written to catch exactly that said OK throughout.
why_gates_miss_it: This IS the gate. It is the only runtime check on the RateLimit-0 denies - the file's own header explains it must be a live test because a template assertion would be "an expectation read from the code under test". Nothing else in the 32 preflight stages reads usage-plan scope; `ChatRouteDenyTests` in backend/tests/test_handlers.py only greps template.yaml text, which is precisely the weaker check this file exists to replace. The gate's blindness is invisible because it exits 0 and prints a success line.
suggested_fix: Assert on the 429 body, which is already in hand: a deny is `{"message":"Too Many Requests"}`, an exhausted quota is `{"message":"Limit Exceeded"}`. Treat `Limit Exceeded` on the batch/chat probes as INDETERMINATE and fail (or loudly WARN and exit non-zero), never as PASS - the same reasoning check 1 already applies to itself. Better still, run the boundary probes with a key whose quota cannot be exhausted by the marketing funnel.

title: The free-tier deny assertions - the ones the code calls load-bearing - have never run, because their env var exists nowhere in the repo
evidence:
`const FREE_KEY = process.env.SKY_SCORE_FREE_TIER_KEY;` (line 172); `if (!FREE_KEY) { console.log('  SKIP  free-tier chat/batch deny - SKY_SCORE_FREE_TIER_KEY not set'); ... }` (lines 173-177). A repo-wide grep for `SKY_SCORE_FREE_TIER_KEY` returns exactly ONE file - this one. It is absent from `.env` (which holds only AWS_PROFILE, EPC_BEARER_TOKEN, SKY_SCORE_API_KEY), absent from `.env.example` (AWS_PROFILE, EPC_BEARER_TOKEN, SKY_SCORE_API_KEY, PLAY_CONSOLE_JSON_KEY, ASC_KEY_ID, ASC_ISSUER_ID, ASC_KEY_FILE_PATH, FASTLANE_SKIP_DOCS, COMPANIES_HOUSE_API_KEY), absent from scripts/preflight.sh and absent from .github/workflows/. Live run with .env sourced:
  SKIP  free-tier chat/batch deny - SKY_SCORE_FREE_TIER_KEY not set
  ...
  OK: the demo key reaches /v1/score and nothing else   EXIT=0
The file's own comment on this block: "this assertion is now load-bearing in a way the demo one is not: if this deny stops working, the free tier is not slightly too generous, it is 1,000,000 scores a month - twice Professional's entire published ceiling, for free."
failure_scenario: The `ScoreFreeUsagePlan` per-method denies (backend/template.yaml lines 540-547) stop working - removed in an edit, or lost to the CloudFormation MethodSettings/Throttle ordering trap the same file documents twice. Free-tier keys are minted by `/v1/signup`, which is UNAUTHENTICATED and needs only an unverified email address, so anyone can hold one. Each such key then reaches POST /v1/score/batch (10,000 requests/month x MAX_BATCH_SIZE 100 = 1,000,000 scores, against Professional's published 1,000,000 ceiling at GBP 499/month) and POST /v1/chat (Bedrock, billed to this account). why_gates_miss_it: The skip is the miss: a stage that vanishes from a report is indistinguishable from one that passed - the exact lesson `--skip-e2e` taught this repo on 2026-08-28, applied here to a security boundary rather than a build stage. `ChatRouteDenyTests` covers only the template text, which the test file itself argues is not evidence. title: /v1/signup writes an unverified third party onto the score-update list, and that write permanently locks the real owner out of self-service API signup
failure_scenario: An attacker scripts POST /v1/signup with `source: consumer` against a list of addresses at the per-route ceiling of 1 RPS (backend/template.yaml:71-74) = 86,400/day. Three effects, all verified above: (a) every unknown address is written into `london-flight-map-signups` as a consented subscriber, kept under 35-day PITR, on a list whose owner never asked to join and whose recorded lawful basis is now false; (b) every one of those people is permanently barred from self-service API signup - the 409 path tells them to contact support, so the B2B funnel is closed for the whole of a target company's staff domain; (c) a single probe distinguishes three states (no record / consumer subscriber / API key holder), so the endpoint is a clean customer-enumeration oracle with a distinguishing message for each.
why_gates_miss_it: `SignupHandlerTests` and `SignupDuplicateNamesTheListTests` in backend/tests/test_handlers.py assert the response WORDING for each duplicate branch - they encode the current behaviour as correct rather than asking whether an unverified third party should be able to create the row that produces it. No preflight stage exercises /v1/signup against the live API at all, and the per-route throttle bounds the RATE, which is the only control the docstring claims. The docstring itself reads as a completed security analysis, which is why nobody re-ran it when the consumer path landed on 2026-08-21.
suggested_fix: Do not persist a consumer address until it is confirmed: write a pending row with a one-time token and only promote it on a click-through, or at minimum stop letting a consumer row block the API-key path (key it on `source`, or use a composite sort key so the two registers are independent rows). Make all three duplicate replies identical and non-committal so the endpoint stops distinguishing register membership. Until confirmation exists, privacy.html section on the score-update list should not claim Article 6(1)(a) consent for every row.

title: /nhs is unauthenticated, holds a Lambda for up to 26 seconds per request, and is the one route with no per-method throttle
evidence:
The `MethodSettings` list (line 52) declares exactly seven ResourcePath entries: `/*`, `/v1/signup`, `/epc`, `/v1/environment`, `/badge`, `/v1/score`, `/v1/score/batch`. `/nhs`, `/transport`, `/sold-prices` and `/favourites` have none, so all four inherit the stage-wide 50 RPS / 100 burst ceiling. `/nhs` is the worst of them: `NhsFunction` (line 228) has `Timeout: 28`, `query_overpass` uses `urlopen(req, timeout=26)` (backend/lambdas/nhs/app.py:210), there is no caching of Overpass results anywhere in the file, and any coordinate outside the bundled London bbox goes straight to live Overpass under the User-Agent `sky-score/1.0 (https://d1oe4ftwutjpf.cloudfront.net)` (app.py:200). Verified unauthenticated live:
  curl '.../prod/nhs?lat=51.47&lon=-0.16'        -> 200 (no key)
  curl '.../prod/transport?lat=51.47&lon=-0.16'  -> 200 (no key, 2.4s)
The template already articulates this exact risk for the sibling route it DID protect (line 88-92, on /epc): "Without this the route inherited the 50 RPS '*/*' ceiling, so an anonymous flood could (a) exhaust the MHCLG quota ... and (b) starve GET /v1/score through the shared stage bucket - the exact failure the 2026-07-24 soak showed." The /v1/environment entry (line 108) adds "a ceiling on how hard an abuser can push a third party using our name". Both arguments apply more strongly to /nhs, which is slower and hits a free community service with a per-IP budget.
failure_scenario: An attacker sends 50 RPS of `GET /nhs?lat=56.5&lon=-4.2` (any coordinate outside the London snapshot bbox, so `in_bundle_area` is false and every request reaches Overpass). Two consequences, neither needing a key: (1) the stage-wide 50 RPS bucket is fully consumed by /nhs, so paying customers' `GET /v1/score` requests are rejected at the gateway with 429 - the noisy-neighbour outage the 2026-07-24 soak was run to find, reproduced from an unauthenticated route; (2) 3,000 Overpass queries a minute leave AWS's shared egress under a User-Agent naming skyscore.co.uk, which is how we get rate-limited or blocked by Overpass - and the Lambda has no Overpass cache, so there is no second line. Each request additionally pins a 256 MB Lambda for up to 26 s, so sustained 50 RPS implies ~1,300 concurrent executions; if that crosses the account concurrency limit, every other function in the stack throttles too (I note the account figure is the part I could not read, so I am asserting only the stage-bucket and Overpass effects as certain).
why_gates_miss_it: No test in the repo reads `MethodSettings` or `ThrottlingRateLimit` - I grepped backend/tests/ and tests/ for both and got zero hits. `ApiGatewayTimeoutCapTests` covers Timeout values only; `demo-key-scope.mjs` covers key-to-route scope, not rate. The four unprotected routes are unauthenticated, so nothing in the key/usage-plan machinery constrains them either. The gap is invisible from the code because the protected routes' entries look like a complete list until you compare it against the Events blocks.
suggested_fix: Add per-method entries mirroring the /epc and /v1/environment precedent - `GET /nhs` and `GET /transport` at roughly 2-5 RPS / 5-10 burst, `GET /sold-prices` similarly, and a modest ceiling on `/favourites` writes. One entry per route only, per the ordered-UpdateStage-patch scar the file already documents. Consider memoising Overpass results on rounded coordinates the way `reverse_geocode` does, so a flood costs one upstream query rather than one per request.

title: OPTIONS /v1/environment requires an API key, so CORS preflight fails 403 with no CORS headers on the route built for public browser callers
evidence:
The `EnvironmentOptions` event (line 451) carries `Auth: ApiKeyRequired: true` (line 458), while the `EnvironmentGet` event immediately above it has no Auth block at all. Verified live:
  OPTIONS /prod/v1/environment  (Origin + Access-Control-Request-Method + Access-Control-Request-Headers)
    -> HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden, x-amzn-ErrorType: ForbiddenException, {"message":"Forbidden"}
    -> and NO Access-Control-Allow-Origin header in the response
  GET /prod/v1/environment?lat=51.47&lon=-0.16  -> 200 (no key)
  OPTIONS /prod/epc  -> 200   (the sibling unauthenticated route, for contrast)
The route's own docstring (backend/lambdas/score/app.py:6970-6974) and the template comment at line 421 both state it is unauthenticated precisely because "the extension is a public artefact ... so a key-gated route is unusable there". The GET honours that; the OPTIONS contradicts it.
failure_scenario: Any browser client that triggers a CORS preflight on this route - i.e. any caller sending a non-safelisted request header, which is the normal shape for a third-party integration and the reason the Api-level `Cors` block sets `AllowOrigin: '*'` - gets a 403 on the preflight with no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, so the browser blocks the actual request and the developer sees an opaque CORS error. The currently-shipped extension escapes only by accident: `background.js` sends `{ Accept: 'application/json' }`, which is CORS-safelisted, so no preflight is issued. suggested_fix: Add /area/ plus a small rotating sample of borough pages (one per city, chosen deterministically) to both PAGES lists, and add `<main>` to the template in scripts/build_area_pages.py. Since the pages are generated from one template, scanning three of them gates all 99.

title: On every phone width the result card's close button is 69% covered by the sticky search card - live in production, on the default mobile layout
evidence: Measured at 390x844 against BOTH the working tree and the live site (https://d1oe4ftwutjpf.cloudfront.net/), after clicking a ranking row so a result renders: `#result-close` rect is top 113, bottom 149, left 341, right 377; `.search-box` rect is top 54, bottom 138. `document.elementFromPoint()` at the button's centre returns DIV.search-box. Sampling the button's own rect on a 2px grid, 90 of 324 points reach it - 27.8% - leaving an exposed strip 36px wide by 11px tall. Identical numbers at 320x568 and 375x667 on live (exposed 90/324, centre hits DIV.search-box at all three). Scrolling does not rescue it: setting #sidebar.scrollTop to scrollHeight puts the button at top -3419 with 0 of 324 points exposed, because `.search-box` is `position: sticky` (index.html:3118-3130, `top: calc(env(safe-area-inset-top) + 54px)`, `z-index: 3`) and stays pinned while `#tab-analysis` scrolls under it. Cause is both geometric and z-order: the sticky offset drags the search card 46px down over `#tab-analysis` (which starts at y=108), and `#tab-analysis` is `position: relative` with `z-index: auto` (index.html:3141-3150) so it creates no stacking context - `.result-close`'s `z-index: 2` (index.html:3167) competes directly with the search box's `z-index: 3` and loses. A screenshot of the live page at 390x844 shows only a sliver of the `×` glyph below the search card. The same run also found `#layers-trigger` and `#legend-toggle` covered by the result card at 320/375/390 (2 of 3 at 844x390). The button is the only dismissal affordance: index.html:13287-13302 is the sole `#result-close` handler and nothing else restores the empty state; `grep -rn 'result-close' tests/` returns nothing.
failure_scenario: A visitor on a phone (tabbed layout is the web default at <=900px since 2026-08-27, index.html:4119) searches a postcode or taps a borough. The result card opens over the map. The `×` that returns them to the map is painted under the floating white search card - visually a stray mark, and a tap at its centre hits the search input instead. Its effective touch target is 36x11px, under the WCAG 2.5.8 24x24 minimum. There is no other way back to a clean map short of reloading the page.
why_gates_miss_it: tests/responsive.mjs has exactly the detector for this (the `covered` block, elementFromPoint at each control's centre) but it only ever audits two page states - the landing state and the legend-open state (tests/responsive.mjs:37-66). Neither renders a result, and `.result-close` is `display: none` until one does (index.html:2977-2979 base rule, plus the `#tab-analysis:has(.empty-state) .result-close { display: none }` rule at index.html:3176), so the detector cannot see the element by construction. tests/a11y-source.mjs DOES reach the borough-selected state at 390x844, but axe has no occlusion rule: a covered button is still rendered, correctly named (`aria-label="Close result and return to map"`) and focusable, so nothing fires. No test in the repo references #result-close.
suggested_fix: Give `#tab-analysis` a `margin-top` that clears the sticky offset (or `z-index: 4` plus a stacking context) so the card's top-right corner is never under `.search-box`; alternatively move `.result-close` below the sticky band. Then add a third state to tests/responsive.mjs - `prepare: 'result'`, clicking a ranking row before the audit - so the covered detector can finally see the state where two-thirds of the mobile chrome lives.

title: Every borough band is weighted by RETIRED postcodes: 39.2% of the sample no longer exists, and the guard that looks like it excludes them removes only 1.25% of them
evidence:
`collect_postcodes()` is the single NSPL pass behind transport, healthcare, road noise, flood and air quality for all 91 boroughs. It never reads NSPL's `doterm` column (date of termination) - `grep -n doterm scripts/build_borough_bands.py` returns nothing. Its only filter is lines 266-268:

    # NSPL parks terminated/unlocatable postcodes at (99.999, 0.0).
    if lat > 90 or lat < -90:
        continue

That comment is the defect: it reads as "terminated postcodes are excluded" and the test excludes only UNLOCATABLE ones. Measured over the whole 2,723,596-row data/nspl.csv: 915,867 rows are terminated, of which only 11,414 (1.25%) sit at lat>90; **904,453 terminated postcodes carry real coordinates and pass straight through**. (12,789 LIVE postcodes are also parked at lat>90, which is what the parking rule is actually about.) Sampled rows confirm it - E09000019 (Islington) contains `EC1A 1TD doterm=201812 lat 51.524567 lon -0.112017` and `EC1A 1XA doterm=201812` at the identical coordinate.

Across the twelve cities the script derives, 373,642 of 952,582 sampled postcodes (39.2%) are terminated - London 45.5%, Cardiff 58.2%, Leicester 35.1%.

The repo already knows what "live" means and disagrees with itself: backend/lambdas/score/app.py:4263 records "180,983 live London postcode centroids", and my live-only London count is **exactly 180,983** while build_borough_bands.py uses 332,308. Two sibling scripts in the same directory filter the column explicitly - scripts/build_city_neighbourhoods.py:669 (`c_term = cols.get('doterm')`, docstring: "including them would drag a centroid toward wherever the estate used to be") and scripts/build_aircraft_quiet_dataset.py:152.

I re-ran the script's own `transport_share()`, `sample_aq()`, `sample_raster()` and `sample_codes()` over the same points, once with all postcodes and once live-only. The all-postcode column reproduces data/borough-extra.json EXACTLY (Camden transport 98.5, Leicester 26.7, Kingston flood 20.02, Islington road 75.3, Bath and NE Somerset transport 25.8), which proves the reproduction is faithful. Live-only changes the PUBLISHED BAND for **27 boroughs on transport, 22 on road noise, 5 on flood and 1 on air quality**.
failure_scenario: Leicester's `transportWithin800mPct` is published as 26.7% and banded `moderate`; over live postcodes only it is 12.0% and bands `poor`. Hinckley and Bosworth 22.5% -> 10.5%. Bath and North East Somerset 25.8% -> 16.9% (`moderate` -> `poor`). Transport is 0.25 of the liveability component in BOTH holders, so the wrong band is served by /v1/score and rendered by the site identically. Feeding the corrected bands through `resolve_query` moves published headline scores: Ealing `live` 8.3 -> 7.6 and score 5.7 -> 5.5; Richmond upon Thames 5.0 -> 4.8; Bexley 8.6 -> 8.4; Enfield 8.4 -> 8.2. On the v4.0 environment inputs: Islington's `roadNoiseAboveWhoPct` 75.3 -> 65.1 (band `high` -> `moderate`), Redbridge 72.1 -> 62.0, Richmond 68.6 -> 56.7, and Kingston upon Thames's `floodMediumOrHighPct` 20.02 -> 5.69 (band `high` -> `medium`). The bias is not random: retired postcodes cluster in redeveloped inner-urban blocks near stations (and duplicate a single coordinate many times, as the two EC1A rows show), so transport access is systematically over-stated where churn is highest.
why_gates_miss_it: `build_borough_bands.py --check` (the advisory `borough bands == sources` stage) re-derives from the same NSPL with the same inclusion rule, so it compares the file against itself and prints "borough-extra.json agrees with DEFRA on every derived field" - I ran it and it passed. `tests/test_borough_data_parity.py` compares borough-extra.json against the Lambda's CITIES, and `--write-lambda`/`--sync-lambda` copy the same number into both, so both holders hold the same wrong value and the parity gate is green by construction. `tests/borough-score-parity.mjs` compares the score the SITE renders against the Lambda's - both computed from that same input. `tests/layer-honesty.mjs` asserts only that a borough with a reading is painted and one without is not; a wrong reading is still a reading. `scripts/check_score_sanity.py` asserts discrimination and range, never whether a share is correct. Nothing in the 32 stages ever compares a live-postcode count with an all-postcode count.
suggested_fix: Read `doterm` in `collect_postcodes()` and skip any row where it is non-empty, exactly as build_city_neighbourhoods.py:669 and build_aircraft_quiet_dataset.py:152 already do; correct the comment at line 266, which describes locatability and not termination. Then re-run `--write --write-lambda` and re-run build_area_pages.py --write, since 55 band values across 91 boroughs move. Consider extracting the one NSPL row filter into a shared helper so the three scripts cannot disagree about what a postcode is again.

title: The EA flood mosaic misregisters every city's edge tiles: partial tiles are rendered at 2000x2000 px whatever their extent, then placed as if they were 10 m/px, stretching real flood polygons by up to 5x
evidence:
`fetch_tile()` always asks the WMS for a fixed-size image regardless of how big the bbox is - line 156: `raw = fetch_bytes(getmap_url(bbox, TILE_PX, TILE_PX))` with TILE_PX = 2000. The tile grid at lines 216-222 clamps the last row and column: `e2, n2 = min(e + TILE_M, bbox[2]), min(n + TILE_M, bbox[3])`, so edge tiles cover less than 20 km but are still rendered into 2000 px. The mosaic at lines 234-243 then assumes a uniform `res = TILE_M // TILE_PX` = 10 m/px for every tile.

Every city has partial edge tiles - `city_bbox()` rounds to 1 km, not 20 km. Measured spans: London 64000x51000 (remainder 4000x11000), Leicester 69000x71000 (9000x11000), Merseyside 49000x51000 (9000x11000), Tyne and Wear 38000x37000 (18000x17000). All 103 cached .npy tiles are 4,000,128 bytes = 2000x2000 + header, confirming edge tiles are the same pixel size as full ones.

Proved three independent ways, entirely offline:
1. Placement: for London, `mosaic[0:2000, 0:2000]` is byte-identical to flood_501000_193000.npy (a tile covering only N 193000-204000, 11 km) while the mosaic transform claims those rows span N 184000-204000, 20 km; `mosaic[2000:3100]` equals `mid[900:2000]`, i.e. the correctly-placed mid tile was partly overwritten by the stretched top tile.
2. Anisotropy: mean vertical/horizontal run-length of risk pixels is 0.95-1.07 in the four full 20x20 km tiles (isotropic, as expected), 1.49-1.68 in the three London top-row tiles (11 km tall rendered into 2000 px -> predicted 1.82x vertical stretch) and 0.25-0.36 in the two east-column tiles (4 km wide into 2000 px -> predicted 5x horizontal stretch).
3. Adjacency: the top tile's bottom 900 rows share only 4.8% Jaccard overlap with the mid tile's top 900 rows over 164,972 risk pixels - they are not the same ground, so the mosaic's 20 km assumption is refuted.

Re-sampling the cached tiles with each tile's own true resolution and comparing against the current mosaic: **37 of 81 boroughs' `floodMediumOrHighPct` is wrong and 13 boroughs' published `flood` band is wrong.**
failure_scenario: Sefton (Merseyside) publishes `floodMediumOrHighPct: 31.39` and `flood: "high"` - the highest flood figure in the whole dataset. Correctly georeferenced it is 0.28%, i.e. `low`. South Tyneside publishes 10.94 (`high`); correct value 0.09 (`low`). Doncaster 24.38 (`high`) vs 6.38 (`medium`). Bury 8.51 (`medium`) vs 0.78 (`low`). Also wrong-banded: South Gloucestershire, Melton, Enfield, Hackney, Hillingdon, Newham, Redbridge, Barnsley, Gateshead. Two consequences, both live: the map paints those boroughs in the wrong flood colour under a legend that says the data is measured, and since v3.9/v4.0 `floodMediumOrHighPct` is a scored input (0.20 of `environment`) held in BOTH score holders. Running the corrected values through the Lambda's own `get_env_score`/`resolve_query`: Sefton environment 5.40 -> 7.30 and headline 5.5 -> 5.8; South Tyneside 5.20 -> 7.10 and 7.3 -> 7.6; Bury 5.60 -> 7.10 and 7.5 -> 7.7; South Gloucestershire 6.90 -> 7.90 and 7.4 -> 7.6.
why_gates_miss_it: `build_borough_bands.py --check` samples data/ea_flood_risk_<city>.tif - the same mosaic - so it re-derives the identical wrong number and reports agreement; I ran it and it printed "borough-extra.json agrees with DEFRA on every derived field". Both score holders carry that number, so `tests/test_borough_data_parity.py` and `tests/borough-score-parity.mjs` compare two copies of it. `tests/layer-honesty.mjs` only checks that a borough with a reading gets painted. The script's own `--verify` mode checks the colour-to-band mapping at a single 8 km sample near Ipswich and never looks at the tiling geometry at all, and it needs the network so it is in no preflight stage. The `nz == 0` guard added at line 185 catches a wholly blank tile but a stretched tile is full of real classified pixels. Nothing in the repo has ever compared the mosaic back to the EA service's own `risk_band`.
suggested_fix: Request each tile at its true size - `getmap_url(bbox, (e2-e)//res, (n2-n)//res)` - or, better, pad the bbox in `city_bbox()` up to a whole multiple of TILE_M so every tile is full-size, and assert `codes.shape == ((n2-n)//res, (e2-e)//res)` before writing it into the mosaic so a mismatch fails loudly. Delete the affected cached tiles, refetch, then re-run `build_borough_bands.py --write --write-lambda` and `build_area_pages.py --write`. Worth adding a preflight-able check that samples a handful of postcodes from the mosaic and compares against the WMS GetFeatureInfo `risk_band`, which is the only thing that can catch a geometry fault in a decoded image.

title: roadNoiseAboveWhoPct is a share of the postcodes DEFRA mapped, not of the borough's addresses, but is published and scored as the latter - the quiet cells are dropped from the denominator
evidence:
`sample_raster()` at line 307 keeps only positive cells - `good = np.isfinite(vals) & (vals > 0)` - and its docstring says values of 0 or nodata mean "below the lowest mapped band, which is an absence of noise". `derive()` then computes the exposure share over the SURVIVORS at line 608:

    exposed = 100.0 * float((vals >= WHO_ROAD_LDEN_DB).sum()) / vals.size
    ...
    rec['roadNoiseCoverage'] = round(100 * vals.size / len(points), 1)

so `roadNoiseCoverage` records exactly the fraction that was dropped, and nothing uses it. The dropped cells really are quiet, not unmodelled-and-unknowable: reading data/defra_road_lden_westmidlands.tif directly, 0.0% of cells carry the declared nodata (-96.0), 17.9% are exactly 0, and the positive values start at 40.0 dB - the bottom of DEFRA's mapped range and 13 dB below the 53 dB WHO cut. A cell at 0 is therefore certainly below the guideline and belongs in the denominator as not-exposed.

The published definition says otherwise. backend/lambdas/score/app.py:5376 - "Road noise 0-10 from the share of postcodes at or above WHO 53 dB Lden"; app.py:5304 - "100% = every address in the borough at or above WHO's 53 dB Lden"; the module docstring here (line 32) - "Banded on the SHARE OF ADDRESSES at or above the WHO 2018 guideline".

Because the published value is exactly true_share / (coverage/100), the error is computable for every borough: coverage runs 88.0% (Solihull) to 100% (London), so published values are overstated by up to 5.5 percentage points.
failure_scenario: Solihull publishes `roadNoiseAboveWhoPct: 45.7` with `roadNoiseCoverage: 88.0`; the share of its addresses over the WHO guideline is 40.2%. Every one of the 86 boroughs with road data is biased in the same direction - louder, i.e. worse - by 0 to 5.5 points. One published map band is wrong as a result: London's Sutton is banded `moderate` road noise at 50.2%, and the corrected 49.7% falls under the 50% cut and bands `low`. Since v4.0 the field also scores at 0.35 of `environment`, so environment is understated by up to 0.2 (Solihull 7.5 -> 7.7, Harborough 7.7 -> 7.8, Melton 7.1 -> 7.2, North Somerset 8.2 -> 8.3), roughly 0.03 on a headline score.
why_gates_miss_it: Identical self-agreement to the two findings above: `build_borough_bands.py --check` recomputes the share the same way and reports agreement, and both score holders receive the same value via `--write` / `--write-lambda`, so the parity and site-vs-Lambda gates compare two copies of it. No gate anywhere reads `roadNoiseCoverage`, and no gate compares the published definition string in app.py against what the script computes.
suggested_fix: Divide by `len(points)` rather than `vals.size` at line 608 so the denominator is the borough's postcodes, matching the definition the API publishes - keeping `roadNoiseCoverage` as the disclosure of how much of the borough carried a mapped value. If the intent is instead to score only the mapped fraction, then app.py:5304/5376 and the docstring here need to say "share of the postcodes DEFRA mapped", and boroughs below some coverage floor should decline the input rather than publish a share of a subset.

title: The native bundle's data allow-list is still the four files it had on 3 August, so a Capacitor build ships without 9 of 11 cities' boundaries and every font in the atomic precache set
evidence:
copy-web.mjs:102 declares the complete data allow-list:

  const REQUIRED_DATA = [
    'borough-extra.json',
    'london-boroughs.json',
    'nyc-boroughs.json',
    'aircraft-noise-london-lden.png',
  ];

and the only directories copied are icons/, js/ and prototype/ (lines 74-84). fonts/ is copied nowhere.

I reproduced the copier's rules against sw.js's SHELL_ASSETS with node (read-only):
  SHELL_ASSETS entries: 20
  NOT copied into mobile/www by copy-web.mjs: 12
     /data/manchester-boroughs.json, /data/westmidlands-boroughs.json,
     /data/westyorkshire-boroughs.json, /data/southyorkshire-boroughs.json,
     /data/merseyside-boroughs.json, /data/tyneandwear-boroughs.json,
     /data/bristol-boroughs.json, /data/leicester-boroughs.json,
     /data/teesside-boroughs.json,
     /fonts/fonts.css, /fonts/inter.woff2, /fonts/jetbrains-mono.woff2

The last-built bundle on disk confirms it, not just my model of it: `ls mobile/www` shows no fonts/ directory at all, and `ls mobile/www/data` shows exactly aircraft-noise-london-lden.png, borough-extra.json, london-boroughs.json, nyc-boroughs.json.

Dates (git log): the allow-list landed 2026-08-03 (3b31ca9). Fonts joined SHELL_ASSETS 2026-08-06 (daa7270), Manchester 2026-08-09 (1d8c67e), six regions 2026-08-10, Leicester and Teesside 2026-08-11 (601d89e). Every entry it misses was added after it was written.

sw.js:290 is `cache.addAll(SHELL_ASSETS)` — atomic. index.html:8175 loadCityBoundaries catches a failed fetch and returns [] with a console.warn. index.html:7718 catches a failed aircraft-quiet fetch with `console.warn('aircraft-quiet unavailable; using flight-path geometry:', err)`; neither aircraft-quiet file is on the allow-list either.
failure_scenario: Codemagic's ios-workflow runs `npm run build:web` (codemagic.yaml:67). copy-web.mjs finds all four of its listed files, prints `done`, exits 0, and the build proceeds. In the resulting app: (1) a user taps the Greater Manchester chip and gets "Greater Manchester borough outlines could not be loaded" — the same for West Midlands, West Yorkshire, South Yorkshire, Merseyside, Tyne and Wear, Bristol, Leicester and Teesside, i.e. 9 of the 11 cities on the switcher; (2) `cache.addAll` rejects on the first missing entry, so the service worker never installs and the app has no offline shell at all — the exact atomic-failure mode the file's own comment cites for nyc-boroughs.json; (3) /data/aircraft-quiet-london.json and /data/aircraft-quiet-regions.json 404 inside the bundle, so every postcode result scores aircraft quiet from flight-path geometry while /v1/score answers the same postcode from the DEFRA raster — the site/API divergence the Makefile's data-deploy comment calls "LOAD-BEARING FOR CORRECTNESS", reopened for 42,691 measured postcodes, with a console.warn on a phone as the only signal.
why_gates_miss_it: Nothing runs copy-web.mjs outside the cloud build. I grepped preflight.sh, package.json, Makefile, .github/workflows and codemagic.yaml for copy-web / REQUIRED_DATA / build:web: the only hits are codemagic.yaml:67 and mobile/package.json:7. None of preflight's 32 stages touches the mobile bundle, and no test compares REQUIRED_DATA against SHELL_ASSETS or against index.html's /data/ fetches. The allow-list was introduced precisely to replace an extension filter that "fails open: add a file, get no error, ship without it" — but a STATIC allow-list fails closed only for the files already on it; adding a twelfth boundary file still produces a green build.
suggested_fix: Derive the copy set instead of listing it: parse SHELL_ASSETS out of sw.js and the /data/ literals out of index.html at build time, copy exactly that union (fonts/ included), and fail the build if any SHELL_ASSETS entry is absent under www/ after the copy. That makes the mobile bundle re-derive itself whenever a city is added, which is the event that broke it three times over.

title: /v1/environment and /badge publish DEFRA measurements with no sources array, so the extension panel's own attribution footer credits everyone except DEFRA — while LICENSING.md asserts no such code path exists
evidence:
handle_environment's response (app.py:7088-7096) carries exactly five keys:

  return response(200, {
      'location': {...}, 'environment': env, 'notices': notices,
      'apiVersion': API_VERSION, 'methodologyVersion': METHODOLOGY_VERSION,
  })

No `sources`. Confirmed live, not just read — I called the running API:
  curl .../prod/v1/environment?lat=51.5074&lon=-0.1278
  top-level keys: ['apiVersion','environment','location','methodologyVersion','notices']
  has sources? -> False
  body includes roadNoiseLdenDb 79.2, no2AnnualMeanUgm3 34.2, pm25AnnualMeanUgm3 11.0
The two `*Source` strings it does carry name the body in prose ("DEFRA Strategic Noise Mapping Round 4, road Lden") but carry neither the OGL statement nor a link.

handle_badge (app.py:7195-7231) is the same: _badge_svg emits SKY SCORE, the score, /10, the band label and the postcode, and nothing else. I checked programmatically which public handlers reference sources at all: handle_badge False, handle_environment False, handle_regions False, handle_changes True.

The consumer proves the consequence. extension/content/panel.js:1190 renderSources() reads `for (const s of p.data.sources || []) seen.add(s)` over every payload, and `if (!seen.size) return null`. Its comment says "The Lambdas already return the correct strings in `sources`; our only job is not to drop them" — false for exactly one of its four upstreams. results[] includes environment (panel.js:1386, 1463), so the Environment section contributes nothing to the footer.

LICENSING.md:121-134 is the "Attribution surfacing" table. It lists seven surfaces; /badge and /v1/environment appear in neither it nor anywhere else in the document, though both shipped before LICENSING.md was last edited (2026-08-27). Line 133 then states: "Attribution requirements are structurally satisfied — there is no code path in the API that returns data without the source array."
failure_scenario: A reader opens a Rightmove listing in a postcode with no EPC certificates on record and no Land Registry sales (a new-build, or any of the postcodes where /sold-prices returns an empty array). The only section that resolves is Environment. renderSources() collects zero strings across all payloads, hits `if (!seen.size) return null`, and the panel renders "Road noise 79.2 dB Lden", "NO2 34.2 ug/m3" and "PM2.5 11.0 ug/m3" — all DEFRA, all OGL v3.0 — with no footer and therefore no licence acknowledgement anywhere on the surface. The same holds for any third party integrating the unauthenticated /v1/environment or embedding /badge on a listing page: neither response gives them the OGL statement LICENSING.md's own DEFRA row requires ("Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0"), so the embedder is placed in breach as well, which is the exact reasoning LICENSING.md applies to the bulk CSV export.
why_gates_miss_it: No preflight stage inspects response keys for attribution. `pytest -k every_city_has_its_own_provenance` covers CITY_PROVENANCE on /v1/score only, and tests/test_score_bulk.py::TestAttribution pins the CSV exporter. tests/extension-e2e.mjs asserts the aircraft-quiet inversion against the live endpoint but never asserts a footer. The two surfaces are the two newest public ones (2026-08-06 and 2026-08-21) and were added to no attribution list — the same 'a list of mirrors that omits a mirror reads as complete' shape already recorded for the free-tier quota.
suggested_fix: Have handle_environment and handle_badge run through build_sources() like every other route — the badge can carry a one-line 'OGL v3.0' footer inside the SVG, which also survives the image being hotlinked away from the embedder's page. Then add /badge and /v1/environment to LICENSING.md's surfacing table, and replace line 133's claim with a test that enumerates the public GET handlers and asserts each returns attribution, so the claim can go red instead of ageing.

title: The only gate that compares deployed state to source covers 3 of the 20 assets whose atomic precache decides whether the PWA installs, and prints "all public surfaces match"
evidence:
SURFACES (check_deploy_drift.sh:36-53) is 16 entries: index.html, pricing, privacy, terms, changes, api/, four score-demo files, prototype, robots.txt, sitemap.xml, security.txt, js/api-base.js, fonts/fonts.css.

I intersected it with sw.js's SHELL_ASSETS in python:
  SHELL_ASSETS: 20   SURFACES: 16
  SHELL_ASSETS covered by the drift check: 3 -> ['/', '/index.html', '/fonts/fonts.css']
  NOT covered (17): /manifest.webmanifest, /icons/icon.svg, /icons/icon-maskable.svg,
    /js/vendor/d3.v7.min.js, all 11 boundary JSONs, /fonts/inter.woff2,
    /fonts/jetbrains-mono.woff2
  sw.js itself in SURFACES? False
  any area/ page in SURFACES? False
  any data/ file in SURFACES? False

Line 119 is the success path: printf 'PASS: all %d public surfaces match the live origin.\n' "$CHECKED".

The floor added on 2026-08-23 (lines 94-117) guards the wrong direction: `if [ "$CHECKED" -lt 16 ]` reds when the LIST SHRINKS, and its own comment says "Asserted as a MINIMUM, so adding a seventeenth surface raises it with no edit here" — but nothing raises it, because nothing compares SURFACES to what the Makefile actually deploys. web-deploy-all ships fonts-deploy, web-deploy, data-deploy (17 files), pwa-deploy (4), demo-deploy (7), prototype-deploy, area-deploy (100 files) and meta-deploy — roughly 140 objects, of which 16 are checked.

I confirmed this is a blind spot and not a live failure: I fetched sw.js, data/borough-extra.json, manifest.webmanifest and 12 area pages from CloudFront and SHA-256-compared them against source. All MATCH today.
failure_scenario: `make web-deploy-all` runs. fonts-deploy uploads fonts.css and inter.woff2 but the recursive .woff2 copy is interrupted, or the run hits the documented Git-Bash MSYS invalidation failure that bit on 2026-08-26 *after* the uploads — leaving jetbrains-mono.woff2 absent from the origin. Every later target succeeds. `sh scripts/check_deploy_drift.sh` then compares its 16 surfaces, finds fonts.css present and identical, and prints "PASS: all 16 public surfaces match the live origin". Meanwhile sw.js's cache.addAll(SHELL_ASSETS) rejects on /fonts/jetbrains-mono.woff2, so the service worker fails to install for every visitor of every city — the precise all-or-nothing failure the Makefile warns about in three separate comments — and the one check pointed at the origin says the deploy is complete. The same hole covers a data-deploy that drops one of the nine newer boundary files, and covers all 100 area pages, which bake their scores and whose freshness gate (tests/area-page-freshness.mjs:81, readFileSync) reads LOCAL files against the live API and so can never see a page that did not reach the origin.
why_gates_miss_it: This IS the gate for deployed-vs-source; there is no second one. tests/area-page-freshness.mjs reads the working tree, tests/site-api-parity.mjs compares rendered score against API score on the homepage only, and the responsive/a11y stages were deliberately pointed at SOURCE. Nothing else opens the origin. The count floor at line 117 cannot fire, because the list and the deploy set are two hand-maintained lists that no code compares.
suggested_fix: Build SURFACES from the deploy definitions rather than by hand — at minimum union it with sw.js's SHELL_ASSETS, since those are the entries whose absence is fatal rather than degrading, and add sw.js itself. Then change line 119 to name what it compared ("PASS: 20 of 20 shell assets and N of N public pages") so a shrinking scope is legible in the output, and drop the word "all".

title: The prototype's meta, og and twitter descriptions advertise "live aircraft tracking" on a page whose own live mode is disabled pending OpenSky licensing
evidence:
prototype/index.html:16, :23 and :27:
  <meta name="description" content="Sky Score Radar - 3D terrain visualisation of London airspace with live aircraft tracking, noise contours, and borough boundaries.">
  <meta property="og:description" content="3D terrain visualisation of London airspace with live aircraft tracking, noise contours, and borough boundaries.">
  <meta name="twitter:description" content="3D terrain visualisation with live aircraft tracking and noise contours.">

The same file, line 1805: `const liveLicensed = false;` under a comment headed "*Strong* gate: do NOT just flip liveLicensed to true", and line 2478: `showToast('LIVE MODE DISABLED, AWAITING DATA LICENSING');`. Line 2687 sets the flight panel to 'TRACKED FLIGHTS (SIM)'. The rest of the page has been carefully de-claimed — the airport panel header reads "AIRPORT INTELLIGENCE, EGLL - ILLUSTRATIVE" and the noise panel "DEFRA LDEN, ROUND 4 - 2021 TRAFFIC, ANNUAL AVERAGE, NOT LIVE" — so the three description tags are the residue of that sweep.

The page is publicly indexed: sitemap.xml lists https://skyscore.co.uk/prototype/, and I confirmed prototype/index.html is one of the 16 surfaces check_deploy_drift.sh compares, so the deployed copy carries these tags.
failure_scenario: Someone shares the prototype URL on LinkedIn or X, or it surfaces in a search result. The card and the snippet read "3D terrain visualisation of London airspace with live aircraft tracking" — a capability the page deliberately does not have, and cannot have until OpenSky's written licensing agreement lands (OPENSKY_LICENSING_EMAIL.md, Ticket #835285). A visitor presses the LIVE button the description promised and is told "LIVE MODE DISABLED, AWAITING DATA LICENSING". For a product whose positioning rests on not over-claiming its data, the indexed description is the one surface still making the claim the code was gated to stop making.
why_gates_miss_it: The published-claims dimension enumerated README, METHODOLOGY, CLAUDE, LICENSING, terms, privacy, pricing, api/index.html, score-demo and openapi.yaml — prototype/index.html is not in that list, and no other finder opened it. No preflight stage reads meta descriptions: check_no_em_dash.sh scans the 9 deployed pages for punctuation, a11y-source.mjs scans for WCAG violations, and the drift check compares bytes against the origin without reading them.
suggested_fix: Change all three to describe what the page does — simulated flight tracks over 3D terrain with DEFRA noise contours — and re-run prototype-deploy. Same edit the airport and noise panel headers already received.

title: apple-touch-icon points at an SVG, which iOS Safari does not accept, so Add to Home Screen on the documented iOS PWA path produces a page screenshot instead of the app icon
evidence:
index.html:80:
  <link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="/icons/icon.svg" />

`ls -la icons/` shows the complete web icon set is two SVG files and no raster at any size:
  icon.svg (2,449 bytes), icon-maskable.svg (2,000 bytes)

manifest.webmanifest likewise declares only the same two SVGs, both with "sizes": "any". PNG icons exist only under mobile/assets/ (icon-only.png, icon-foreground.png, icon-background.png, logo.png), which copy-web.mjs does not surface to the web and which are consumed by capacitor-assets for the native target.

I verified all three assets serve correctly from the origin, so this is a format problem and not a deploy problem: /icons/icon.svg 200 image/svg+xml 2449 bytes, /icons/icon-maskable.svg 200 image/svg+xml 2000 bytes, /manifest.webmanifest 200 application/manifest+json 722 bytes — each matching its source byte count.

Apple's touch-icon mechanism has never supported SVG (it takes PNG, conventionally 180x180); when the referenced icon cannot be decoded, iOS substitutes a thumbnail of the page. Chrome does accept an SVG manifest icon with sizes="any", so the Android and desktop install paths are unaffected.
failure_scenario: A visitor on iPhone follows the install path CLAUDE.md documents as one of three ("iOS Safari uses Share -> Add to Home Screen"). Safari cannot decode /icons/icon.svg for the touch icon and falls back to a screenshot of whatever the page was showing at that moment — typically the map mid-render or the search sheet — so the home-screen tile is an unbranded thumbnail rather than the radar-rings mark. This is the same class of defect as the 2026-05-12 App Store 2.3.8 rejection for placeholder icons, on the web install path rather than the native one.
why_gates_miss_it: tests/pwa-check.mjs is referenced only from the Makefile, not from scripts/preflight.sh, so it is in no blocking or advisory stage. No preflight gate reads the manifest or the icon links: a11y-source.mjs scans axe rules, responsive.mjs measures control geometry, and smoke-local.mjs counts the d3 requests. The drift check compares bytes for 16 surfaces and includes neither the manifest nor icons/, so it cannot even tell you the icon is being served.
suggested_fix: Render a 180x180 PNG from icons/icon.svg, point apple-touch-icon at it, and add a 192 and 512 PNG to the manifest alongside the SVGs so Chrome's richer install dialog also has a raster to use. Add both to sw.js SHELL_ASSETS only after they exist at the origin, given cache.addAll is atomic, and wire tests/pwa-check.mjs into preflight so the icon set has a gate at all.
